clue.text: Puzzle — cattle disease grips bird

indicators.note: the disease grips the bird, holding it between its first letter and the rest

parts.note: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease
the emu is a large flightless Australian bird

explanation.surface: A puzzling report of a sick herd of cattle with a bird caught up in it.
explanation.definitionFit: To puzzle someone is to bewilder or perplex them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Orchestras welcoming American Democrat (Liberal) in South Dakota region

indicators.note: the orchestras welcome the others in, taking them inside after their first letter

parts.note: bands are groups of musicians, orchestras in a loose sense
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: Bands in South Dakota play host to a liberal Democrat from America.
explanation.walkthrough: Badlands National Park, with its eroded buttes and canyons, lies in south-western South Dakota.
explanation.definitionFit: The Badlands is the famously eroded, barren terrain of South Dakota, protected as a national park.

clue.text: Roughly shake mate to get a move on

indicators.note: roughly means handled without care, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone shakes a dawdling friend roughly to hurry them along.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning to hurry up and act quickly.

clue.text: Undergo shame surrounding us

indicators.note: the word for shame encloses the clue's own word us, after its first letter

parts.note: a stain on one's character is a disgrace or shame

explanation.surface: We are asked to suffer a disgrace that surrounds us.
explanation.definitionFit: To sustain an injury or loss is to suffer or experience it, a synonym.

clue.text: Jettisons rotten, mostly base publicity items

parts.note: food that is off has gone rotten

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word for base is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: low means base or vulgar
ads are advertisements, items of publicity

explanation.surface: Someone dumps rotten, rather tacky promotional material.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean getting rid of or unloading something unwanted, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Frivolous exploit the lady's intellect emptily engineered

parts.note: a feat is a notable exploit or achievement
her is the possessive for a woman, the lady's
the brain stands for intellect

indicators.note: emptily means the word engineered is emptied of its inside, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A shallow scheme to exploit a woman's mind, mindlessly engineered.
explanation.walkthrough: Emptily also chimes with the empty-headed sense of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is silly and lacking seriousness, hence frivolous.

clue.text: Be vigilant, toilet lock ultimately not in use

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet

indicators.note: ultimately means finally, so only the closing letter of lock is taken

parts.note: out can mean not in use or not in operation

explanation.surface: A warning to stay alert because the lavatory lock no longer works.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch out is to stay alert and watchful, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Make use of a thing that conceals, we're told

indicators.note: we're told signals that what is heard, not what is written, gives the entry

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a veil is a cloth that hides or conceals the face

explanation.surface: Use something that hides things, or so we hear.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail oneself of something is to take advantage of it or use it.

clue.text: Sun at first heats up bodies of bees

indicators.note: at first means only the opening letter of the word Sun is used

parts.note: warms means heats up

explanation.surface: The early sun warms the bees as they gather.
explanation.definitionFit: Swarms are large groups of bees moving together, and bodies here means groups or masses.

clue.text: Regularly admit emphasis on remarkable flare, for example

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of admit is taken, the second and fourth

parts.note: stress is emphasis placed on something
signal as an adjective means notable or remarkable

explanation.surface: An admission given special emphasis about an extraordinary flare.
explanation.walkthrough: Signal as an adjective (a signal victory) means striking or remarkable.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare fired from a ship in trouble is one example of an emergency call for help.

clue.text: Raised fists of Ellington and Wellington?

definitions.meaning: to put up your ... is slang for raising one's fists to fight
Duke Ellington the jazzman and the Duke of Wellington both bore the title

explanation.surface: Two famous figures, one a bandleader and one a general, shown with fists raised.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang word for fists and the title shared by the jazz composer and the victor of Waterloo coincide.

clue.text: Exceptional animator, ace lover

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: A is the card abbreviation for ace

explanation.surface: Praise for a brilliant animator who is also a superb lover.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian-derived word means a female sweetheart or beloved.

clue.text: Three articles right, substantially

parts.note: a, the and a are three articles of grammar, indefinite and definite

explanation.surface: A judgment that three pieces of writing are largely correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means fundamentally or in essence, as does substantially in this sense.

clue.text: Tough outlaw left, facing hesitation

indicators.note: facing means the pieces are placed against each other, side by side in sequence

parts.note: a hood is slang for a gangster or outlaw, as Robin Hood was
um is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: An outlaw who has gone away hesitates before a confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough as a noun is a thug or rough, violent man, a synonym for a hooligan.

clue.text: Total collapse is sadly disorientating

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of disorientating are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complete breakdown is regrettably confusing.
explanation.definitionFit: Falling apart completely into fragments is total collapse or breakdown.

clue.text: Eccentric relations, those from the Far East?

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or out of line, so the letters of relations are rearranged

explanation.surface: Odd family members, perhaps from far-off Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this old-fashioned term for East Asian people is dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The term historically denoted people from East Asia, the region called the Far East.

clue.text: Incites havoc, a truly fragile thing

parts.note: eggs, as in eggs on, means incites or urges
hell can mean chaos or havoc

explanation.surface: Someone stirs up trouble and chaos, a really delicate situation.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin shell of a bird's egg is a byword for fragility, as in walking on eggshells.

clue.text: Building anew, deplorably cutting corners

indicators.note: deplorably implies something done badly, so the letters of cutting corners are rearranged

explanation.surface: A builder rebuilding something while shamefully skimping on quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebuilding something that was damaged or destroyed is constructing it again.

clue.text: Old renegade working to support independent speech

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the one it supports, so it follows

parts.note: a rat is a deserter or traitor, a renegade
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A former turncoat now works to back an independent's address.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public speech or address.

clue.text: Insincere talk advanced with thanks for choral work

parts.note: cant is hypocritical or insincere talk
ta is British informal speech for thank you

explanation.surface: Insincere chatter followed by thanks for a choir's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a composition for voices and instruments, often sung by a choir.

clue.text: A group of directors at sea perhaps

parts.note: a company's board is its group of directors

explanation.surface: A company's directors are at a loss, all at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: At sea in the surface means confused; in the definition it means on a ship, and perhaps covers trains and planes too.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on a ship at sea is one example of being on board a vessel.

clue.text: Kind of rice; a bit ma's cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A type of rice, a little of which mother has cooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Basmati is a long-grain fragrant rice from South Asia.

clue.text: Pleasant little drink with queen

parts.note: a sup is a small mouthful of drink
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: A nice small drink taken in the company of the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal for very good, enjoyable or delightful.

clue.text: Some cricket starts with appeal ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the word for appeal is left out of the word for starts

parts.note: beginnings are starts
to beg is to appeal or plead

explanation.surface: A cricket match gets going with a bowler's appeal disregarded by the umpire.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an appeal is the fielders' shout asking the umpire to give a batter out; an innings is one side's or player's turn to bat.
explanation.definitionFit: An innings is a single spell of batting, a portion of a cricket match.

clue.text: Scotsman caught breaking into fruit machine

indicators.note: breaking into means the other pieces go inside the word for the fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
Ian is a typical Scottish man's name, the Scots form of John
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A Scot is nabbed after breaking into a fruit machine.
explanation.walkthrough: A fruit machine is the British name for a slot machine, which lures the solver to see the fruit and machine as one.
explanation.definitionFit: An appliance is a device or machine for a household task.

clue.text: A step at full tilt

parts.note: a pace is a single step

explanation.surface: A stride taken at top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace means swiftly, at great speed, just as at full tilt does.

clue.text: Adventurously hanging round centre of Hebrides

indicators.note: round means the word for hanging goes around the other piece

parts.note: dangly means hanging loosely

indicators.note: centre of means the two middle letters of Hebrides are taken

explanation.surface: Someone boldly dangling around in the heart of the Scottish islands.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hebrides are islands off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with boldness and courage is acting adventurously.

clue.text: Girl checks email on vacation

parts.note: dams hold back or check a flow of water

indicators.note: on vacation means the word email is vacated, its middle emptied to leave the outside letters

explanation.surface: A young woman checks her inbox while on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an archaic or literary word for a young unmarried woman.
